title: Pest Control Treatment Estimate Worksheet
subtitle: Residential Pest-Control Treatment: prices observed scope, options, and exclusions.
description: Pest Control Treatment Estimate Worksheet covers target pest, activity zone, entry point, treatment location, and contributing condition. The residential pest-service coordinator records Residential Pest-Control Treatment observed scope, costs, options, and terms. Pest Control Treatment Estimate Worksheet keeps Residential Pest-Control Treatment exceptions visible until the residential pest-service coordinator handoff.
use_case: Use Pest Control Treatment Estimate Worksheet at residence, room, exterior perimeter, attic, crawlspace, and occupied area. Document target pest, activity zone, entry point, treatment location, and contributing condition identity before Residential Pest-Control Treatment begins. Compare target pest, activity zone, entry point, treatment location, and contributing condition findings with stated Residential Pest-Control Treatment criteria; route unresolved Residential Pest-Control Treatment issues to licensed or otherwise qualified pest-control reviewer. For Pest Control Treatment Estimate Worksheet, confirm requirements for Residential Pest-Control Treatment. Ask licensed or otherwise qualified pest-control reviewer to review Residential Pest-Control Treatment conditions beyond the residential pest-service coordinator's role.

sections.title: Property estimate review and customer identity
sections.guidance: Identify the customer, asset or property, estimator, and basis date before pricing the work.

blocks.label: Residential Pest-Control Treatment identity

fields.label: Occupant, pet, sensitive-area, and prior-treatment context

blocks.guidance: Use the Residential Pest-Control Treatment identifier printed on target pest, activity zone, entry point, treatment location, and contributing condition or its linked source record.

sections.title: Pricing options and customer decision inputs
sections.guidance: Price the observable work and options. Keep concealed conditions and unconfirmed quantities out of fixed scope.

blocks.label: Residential Pest-Control Treatment scope observations
items: Activity evidence, count, location, and freshness
Entry, moisture, food, waste, and harborage condition
Device or treatment placement and accessibility
Occupant, child, pet, food, and water exposure boundary
Sanitation, exclusion, and structural action needed
blocks.guidance: Mark what was observed or supplied as estimate input; explain anything material that could not be inspected.

sections.title: Estimate exception and change conditions
sections.guidance: State what could change the price, timing, method, or scope before the customer or responsible party decides.

blocks.label: Conditions that may require a revised estimate or specialist review
items: Target pest cannot be reliably identified
Occupied-area or non-target exposure cannot be controlled
Required preparation or vacancy not completed
Structural or sanitation cause prevents effective treatment
blocks.guidance: Pause Residential Pest-Control Treatment and notify residential pest-service coordinator when identification, exposure control, required preparation, or a contributing condition remains unresolved.
